finding_1_published_marker_gate_is_PROSE.what: The published-marker duplicate-publish guard is mandated for spawned agents but is NOT implemented in any of the three gatherer flows.

evidence.mandate_location: docs/agents/cowork-team/flow/spawn-fanout.md:45 — 'The spawned agent flow MUST claim a published marker BEFORE calling send_telegram' — written in the DISPATCHER's doc, describing what a DIFFERENT agent must do.
evidence.grep_targets: published: → 0 hits across the FULL trees of docs/agents/news-scout/, docs/agents/market-watcher/, docs/agents/alert-commander/ and their agent definitions. task_claim → 0 hits in news-scout and market-watcher flows; alert-commander's single hit is an unrelated commit-mutex reference.
evidence.positive_control: Same grep on docs/agents/unified-agent/flow/ returns 3 hits (chef.md:66,70,763) — the query works and the zero is real, not a broken glob.
evidence.runtime_contradiction: Markers published:news-scout-offhours:2026-07-21 and published:market-watcher-offhours:2026-07-21 nonetheless EXIST, owner_agent=news-scout/market-watcher. So the agents claim a marker no document tells them to claim.
evidence.improvisation_signature: Three markers, three DIFFERENT payload shapes: news-scout {slot,cycle,signals[]}; market-watcher-offhours {site,slot,date_vn}; market-watcher-eod {site,slot}. A spec-driven gate produces one shape. Divergent shapes indicate per-cycle LLM improvisation.

finding_1_published_marker_gate_is_PROSE.therefore: The 'final belt-and-suspenders defense against duplicate Telegram posts' (spawn-fanout.md:72) is non-deterministic for these three slots — its presence depends on what each cycle's model improvises, not on any instruction it reads.
finding_1_published_marker_gate_is_PROSE.not_asserted: Whether these agents CHECK the marker and exit, or merely CLAIM it without gating, is NOT determined — it cannot be read off the flow docs, and I did not observe their runtime. Do not assume either. If they only claim without checking, the guard is decorative and duplicate posts are unprotected; if they do check, note the key is date-scoped (published:<slot>:<YYYY-MM-DD>, ttl 100800=28h) on a slot whose cron is '0 */4 * * *' = 6 fires/day, which would permit only the FIRST fire of each day to publish. Both branches are defects; they need different fixes. Determine which before scoping.
finding_1_published_marker_gate_is_PROSE.capability_note: This is NOT the dead-code-gate-without-capability class. All three agents hold mcp__gateway__call_tool, so they CAN claim. The instruction is what is missing, not the tool.
finding_1_published_marker_gate_is_PROSE.class: Same family as this session's telemetry-schema finding: a rule that exists only as prose, in a document the actor does not necessarily read, with no enforcement. Prose mandates in a neighbour's doc are not implementations.

finding_2_alert_commander_carries_the_kn.code: git add docs/agent-memory/notebooks/alert-commander.md  THEN  git commit -m "chore(memory/alert-commander): notebook YYYY-MM-DD"
finding_2_alert_commander_carries_the_kn.defect: git add <paths> followed by a BARE git commit does not scope the commit. A bare commit commits the index AS IT STANDS AT COMMIT TIME, so any peer's git add landing in the gap is swept in and attributed to alert-commander's message.
finding_2_alert_commander_carries_the_kn.why_it_matters_now: This repo runs 3+ concurrent committer classes on one shared index. This exact idiom has already produced three documented sweeps (0e28eed23, 84096f617, f05795c3c), one of which committed a developer's in-progress script as if finished.
finding_2_alert_commander_carries_the_kn.live: alert-commander was SPAWNED by this tick at 20:07Z and will reach this step when it writes its notebook. The defect is armed right now.
finding_2_alert_commander_carries_the_kn.fix: Commit WITH pathspecs: git commit -F - -- docs/agent-memory/notebooks/alert-commander.md. The pathspec form resolves paths into a scratch index before the hook runs and is structurally immune (verified by harness scripts/audits/verify-commit-sweep-discriminator.sh, VERDICT PASS).
finding_2_alert_commander_carries_the_kn.scope_note: Existing row FIX-COMMIT-PATH-PEER-INDEX-SWEEP-GUARD (P0) owns the systemic guard. This is an additional CALLSITE for that row's sweep, not a new row. Grep every agent flow for the add-then-bare-commit idiom while that row is open rather than fixing this one file.
finding_2_alert_commander_carries_the_kn.RETRACTION_20260721T2013Z: WRONG CLASSIFICATION — corrected after the agent returned. This is NOT a live TOCTOU callsite. alert-commander's frontmatter (.claude/agents/alert-commander.md:5) grants exactly 'Read, Write, Edit, mcp__gateway__call_tool' — NO Bash. The agent CANNOT execute git at all, so the bare-commit line has never run and can never run. My 'the defect is armed right now' claim was false; I predicted a sweep from a callsite that is structurally unreachable.
finding_2_alert_commander_carries_the_kn.corrected_class: DEAD PROSE IN AN UNGRANTED TOOL — same class as tran-ngoc-bau's published-marker gate (feedback_router_intent_path_double_dispatches_cowork_slots: 'a gate written in a tool the agent doesn't have is DEAD CODE'). The flow reads as if it commits; it never does.
finding_2_alert_commander_carries_the_kn.confirmed_consequence: alert-commander self-reported at 20:11Z: 'Notebook updated ... written but not committed (no Bash this session)'. Verified: git status showed ' M docs/agent-memory/notebooks/alert-commander.md'. Same for news-scout and market-watcher — all three cowork agents spawned this tick are Bash-less. Their notebooks accumulate UNCOMMITTED, which makes them sweep-bait for the next peer bare-commit. So the bare-commit defect still bites this agent — as a VICTIM, not as a perpetrator.
finding_2_alert_commander_carries_the_kn.corrected_fix: Do NOT rewrite the git block to use pathspecs — an unexecutable instruction stays unexecutable either way. Either (a) grant Bash, or (b) delete the git block and make the dispatcher's commit step explicit + mandatory for Bash-less spawns. Router committed all three on their behalf at 20:13Z (e8b609f74, pathspec-scoped, 4 files, verified via git show --name-status).
finding_2_alert_commander_carries_the_kn.scoping_impact: REMOVE this from FIX-COMMIT-PATH-PEER-INDEX-SWEEP-GUARD's callsite list. Counting an unreachable line inflates that P0's blast radius. It belongs on a Bash-less-agent-cannot-self-commit row instead.

finding_3_no_last_fired_writer_script_ex.what: last-fired.md specifies a batched read/update/atomic-rename, but no script implements it — every dispatcher tick hand-rolls it. ls scripts/agents-flow/ | grep last|fired → zero hits.
finding_3_no_last_fired_writer_script_ex.history: This hand-rolled operation has TWO recorded defects: a jq needle that clobbered the schedule on multi-slot writes, and a zsh loop that reported write-ok without writing. Both were multi-slot cases; this tick was a three-slot write.
finding_3_no_last_fired_writer_script_ex.this_tick: Performed inline via python3 with explicit post-write verification (slot count 23 before and 23 after; all three slots re-read from disk and confirmed advanced 2026-07-21T16:09:45.000Z -> 2026-07-21T20:08:39.648Z). Clean.
finding_3_no_last_fired_writer_script_ex.actionable: A ~30-line scripts/agents-flow/cowork-last-fired-write.js would retire a step that has failed twice. Deliberately NOT authored here — script creation is developer scope, not the dispatcher's.
finding_3_no_last_fired_writer_script_ex.verification_that_would_have_caught_both: Compare slot COUNT before/after and re-read each updated slot FROM DISK. A write that returns success is not evidence the file is intact.

payload.note: 3 spawns, background per BGFAN-1, issued ONE AT A TIME rather than in a single block — a recorded defect binds the correct agent type to the wrong prompt in multi-dispatch blocks, twice in one turn. Sequential dispatch preserves parallelism (all three run concurrently in background) and costs only dispatch latency. Slot tokens claimed pre-spawn and all three released released:1. Pre-spawn published-marker check applied per this session's 19:45Z chef-evening lesson: these three markers are 3.9h old from COMPLETED runs, not live holders, so unlike chef-evening there was no concurrent-run risk and spawning was correct. Old completed marker != in-flight agent; the discriminator is claim age against agent liveness, not marker existence.

finding_4_news_scout_signal_sector_error.claim: news-scout's own signal file labels PNJ 'gold mining' in .summary — a field routed to unified-agent and alert-commander.
finding_4_news_scout_signal_sector_error.ground_truth: docs/data/stock-classification.json:111 lists PNJ as a peer of MWG/DGW under 'Retail / Electronics'. PNJ is a jewelry retailer/manufacturer, not a miner. Signal file: 2 'mining' hits, 0 'jewel' hits.
finding_4_news_scout_signal_sector_error.why_it_matters: Not a cosmetic label. The causal sign INVERTS: for a miner, gold +1.97% is a revenue tailwind; for a jewelry retailer it is an input-cost MARGIN HEADWIND. A downstream consumer chaining PNJ's liquidity stress to today's gold move would read the direction backwards.
finding_4_news_scout_signal_sector_error.not_asserted: Whether the underlying liquidity finding is sound. The 7-article evidence base and the bearish direction are NOT disputed here — only the sector attribution and any inference that depends on it.
finding_4_news_scout_signal_sector_error.severity: MED — contained to one cycle's artifact, but it propagates by routing, not by filename.
